cycle_time.insight: Cycle time is highly variable, so delivery timing is only moderately predictable. The downward trend suggests the system is improving, but the wide spread between median and upper-tail items means a small set of slow work still dominates customer wait time. lead_time.insight: Stakeholders can plan only with moderate confidence over a roughly 6-8 week horizon, because the typical lead time is much shorter than the worst cases but still uneven. The gap between lead time and cycle time suggests substantial waiting before work starts, not just slow execution once started. That means faster coding alone will not fully solve delivery delay.

executive_summary.headline: The team is carrying too much ageing, blocked, and bug-heavy work through a downstream bottleneck, which makes delivery batchy and hard to predict.
executive_summary.narrative: Work is getting into the system, but it is not moving through at a steady pace. A lot of items wait for long periods near the end of the flow, while some items sit untouched at the front for months. Bugs take a large share of active effort, and new defects are arriving faster than they are being cleared. The result is a delivery process that improves in spots but still accumulates delay and risk. Planning is therefore possible only with caution, because a few slow queues and legacy items dominate the experience.
executive_summary.primary_diagnosis: The system’s main constraint is downstream queueing around review, QA, and release, compounded by poor backlog hygiene and persistent blocked work at the front.
executive_summary.main_caveat: The data shows where work waits and accumulates, but it does not prove the exact causes, such as staffing, policies, or external dependencies.

recommendations.action: Reduce WIP limits and enforce them, especially in Ready for Dev, In Review, QA, and Ready for release.
recommendations.why: High WIP and ageing queues are consistent with long cycle times and batchy throughput.
recommendations.first_step: Agree a hard WIP policy for those columns and review it in the next standup.
recommendations.metric_to_watch: WIP, cycle time, ageing WIP, and time in Ready for release
recommendations.expected_effect: Less queueing, fewer old items, and shorter cycle times.

recommendations.action: Treat Ready for release as a managed queue with explicit ownership and daily triage.
recommendations.why: This is the clearest bottleneck and the largest waiting point in the flow.
recommendations.first_step: Assign an owner to review the release queue daily and remove ambiguity around release prerequisites.
recommendations.metric_to_watch: Time in Ready for release and p85 cycle time
recommendations.expected_effect: Faster finalization and a lower long-tail cycle time.

recommendations.action: Clean up the backlog by reviewing stale New items and closing or revalidating dormant work.
recommendations.why: Large amounts of untouched work distort demand signals and clog intake.

recommendations.metric_to_watch: Stale work count and blocked items in New
recommendations.expected_effect: Sharper prioritisation and less hidden inventory.

recommendations.action: Separate bug handling capacity or introduce a dedicated defect triage lane.
recommendations.why: Bugs consume nearly half of current WIP and create bursty interruption.
recommendations.first_step: Define a daily bug triage slot and reserve a small, visible capacity slice for bug fixes.
recommendations.metric_to_watch: Bug share of WIP, bug completions, and bug net flow
recommendations.expected_effect: Lower bug backlog growth and less disruption to feature work.

recommendations.action: Reduce downstream handoff delays by shrinking review and QA batch sizes.
recommendations.why: Batchy completion and long review/QA waits suggest work is moving in large chunks.
recommendations.first_step: Agree to smaller pull sizes into review/QA and unblock items as soon as they are ready.
recommendations.metric_to_watch: Throughput weekly, zero-completion weeks, and time in In Review/QA
recommendations.expected_effect: Smoother flow and fewer zero-output weeks.

recommendations.action: Create a blocker escalation process with clear owners and deadlines.
recommendations.why: Blocked items are stuck for long periods, especially in New.
recommendations.first_step: Add an SLA for blocked items and require an owner plus next action for each one.
recommendations.metric_to_watch: Currently blocked count, total days lost to blocking, and blocker timeline
recommendations.expected_effect: Less time lost to unresolved dependencies.

recommendations.action: Use release readiness criteria to prevent items from sitting half-finished at the end of the flow.
recommendations.why: A lot of ageing accumulates near release, suggesting items enter the final queue before they are truly ready.
recommendations.first_step: Define a strict release-ready checklist and enforce it before items enter that column.
recommendations.metric_to_watch: Ageing in Ready for release and arrival/departure ratio there
recommendations.expected_effect: Fewer old release items and less downstream congestion.

recommendations.action: Inspect the few oldest active items individually and either finish, split, or retire them.
recommendations.why: A small number of very old items appear to dominate the worst tail of delay.

recommendations.metric_to_watch: p85 age, p85 cycle time, and count of items over 30 days

data_quality_caveats: The window is only 6 months, so trends may be influenced by one-off events or recent process changes.
Several charts are based on small samples for certain item types, especially spikes and some lead-time subgroups.
Throughput includes many zero-completion weeks, which makes averages less representative of day-to-day flow.
Some item-level age and blocked metrics reflect current snapshots, not the full history of how long items spent in each state.
The summary is anonymised and does not include team capacity, staffing, release calendar, or dependency data, which limits causal conclusions.
Stale-work and blocked-item lists are very long, but the summary does not say which items are still truly active versus legacy noise.
